# 2025 Tour Championship

The 2025 Tour Championship, held at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta, Georgia, marked a pivotal moment in professional golf history as the season-ending championship of the 2024–2025 PGA TOUR season , . This edition was defined by a landmark structural reversal, reverting to a traditional 72-hole stroke-play format where all 30 competitors began on even par, effectively eliminating the controversial "Starting Strokes" system that had been in place since 2019 , . This change represented a conscious return to a level-playing field, aiming to simplify the competition and enhance its prestige as the ultimate test of season-long performance . The culmination of this reformed playoff structure saw English golfer Tommy Fleetwood secure his first-ever PGA Tour victory with a commanding three-shot triumph over a formidable group of challengers, including Patrick Cantlay and Russell Henley , . His victory was not only a personal breakthrough but also a historic achievement, as he became the first player since Tiger Woods in 2007 to win both the Tour Championship and the FedEx Cup in their maiden PGA Tour title . The tournament concluded on Sunday, August 24, 2025, after four days of intense competition that showcased the highest stakes in professional golf under a new and more straightforward set of rules , .

## A Return to Tradition: The Reversion from Starting Strokes

The most defining characteristic of the 2025 Tour Championship was its deliberate departure from a six-year experiment with a staggered-start format, marking the first time since 2018 that the event reverted to a standard 72-hole stroke-play competition , . For the preceding six seasons, from 2019 through 2024, the finale of the FedExCup Playoffs utilized a complex system known as "Starting Strokes" . Under this model, the top 30 players in the FedEx Cup standings after the BMW Championship began the tournament at different scores based on their ranking . The number one seed started at 10-under-par, the second-ranked player at 8-under, the third at 7-under, the fourth at 6-under, and the fifth at 5-under , . Players ranked sixth through tenth began at 4-under, eleventh through fifteenth at 3-under, sixteenth through twentieth at 2-under, twenty-first through twenty-fifth at 1-under, and the final five qualifiers, ranked twenty-sixth through thirtieth, started at even par , . This innovative but highly debated system was designed to inject drama and create opportunities for lower-ranked players to capture the FedEx Cup, regardless of their regular-season form . However, it generated considerable confusion among fans and criticism from within the player ranks, who argued that it undermined the meritocratic principle of identifying the best player over 72 holes , .

The decision to abandon the "Starting Strokes" format was driven by a confluence of factors stemming from extensive consultation and feedback. Player dissatisfaction was a primary catalyst. Multiple prominent figures voiced their opposition, describing the system as "gimmicky," "kind of wonky," and "not a great way to identify someone who has played well all year" . Even reigning 2024 FedEx Cup champion Scottie Scheffler publicly criticized the format, calling it "silly" and expressing a clear preference for a more traditional competition where the lowest aggregate score determines the winner , . Fan feedback also played a crucial role, indicating a strong desire for a simpler, more straightforward format that produced winning scores closer to par and made it easier for audiences to follow the competition , . The core issue was that winning the tournament under the old system did not always equate to shooting the best 72-hole score; a prime example occurred in 2024 when Collin Morikawa recorded the lowest 72-hole score in the field, yet Scottie Scheffler won due to his significant starting advantage .

In response to this widespread feedback, the PGA Tour officially announced the elimination of the "Starting Strokes" format for the 2025 edition of the Tour Championship , . This decision was part of a broader strategic initiative dubbed "Fan Forward," which aimed to evaluate and enhance the viewing experience across the entire PGA Tour schedule , . PGA Tour Commissioner Jay Monahan stated that the goal was to deliver "the most competitive golf in the world, played for the highest stakes, in the most straightforward and engaging format" . The policy change was ratified during joint meetings of the Board of Directors and the Player Advisory Council (PAC) on July 16, 2025, and officially announced in May 2025 , . The formal announcement confirmed that for the 2025 season, all 30 qualified players would begin the 72-hole stroke-play event at even par, ensuring that the player with the lowest total score over four rounds would be crowned both the tournament champion and the FedEx Cup winner , . This reversion to tradition was intended to restore the integrity and prestige of the FedEx Cup, making the Tour Championship the ultimate and most difficult tournament to win on the PGA Tour calendar , .

## The Event: Venue, Field, and Course Conditions

The 2025 Tour Championship was contested at the storied East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta, Georgia, a venue that has hosted the season-finale annually since 2007 , , . The tournament took place from August 21 to August 24, 2025, serving as the culminating event of the FedExCup Playoffs , . The field consisted of the top 30 players in the FedEx Cup standings following the conclusion of the BMW Championship, a format consistent with recent editions of the playoffs , . This ensured that the strongest performers of the postseason gathered for the final battle for the $10 million FedEx Cup bonus . The official qualifier list provided a snapshot of the elite talent competing, featuring a mix of established superstars, past champions, and rising stars , . Notable names included defending champion Scottie Scheffler, who entered the week ranked first in the FedEx Cup standings ; Northern Irishman Rory McIlroy, a three-time FedEx Cup winner; American Justin Thomas, a two-time runner-up at East Lake; and Canadian Corey Conners , . The field also contained seven players making their debut appearance at the Tour Championship, adding an element of unpredictability to the competition .

In preparation for the 2025 event, the PGA Tour Rules Committee implemented a more challenging course setup at East Lake, a deliberate move to counteract the extremely low scoring seen in recent years . The course renovation prior to the 2024 tournament had already altered the layout, and for 2025, officials aimed to increase risk/reward opportunities and produce winning scores closer to par , . This was a direct response to recent victories where winners posted scores of 20-under par or better, such as Scottie Scheffler's 20-under performance in 2024 , . Despite these adjustments, the tournament was ultimately characterized by soft course conditions resulting from rain, which created receptive greens and facilitated aggressive play, allowing players to attack pins and post impressive scores throughout the week . This combination of a demanding setup and favorable weather created a dynamic environment where both strategy and execution were paramount.

## The Final Four Days: A Narrative of Contention and Victory

The 2025 Tour Championship unfolded as a compelling narrative of high-stakes golf, built around a dramatic two-way battle between Tommy Fleetwood and Patrick Cantlay that dominated the final 36 holes . After 54 holes of play on Saturday, August 23, 2025, the leaderboard was tightly packed, with Fleetwood and Cantlay sharing the lead at a remarkable 16-under-par 194 , . Their position gave them a two-shot cushion over a trio of other elite players: Russell Henley, Keegan Bradley, and Cameron Young, who were all tied for third at 14-under-par . Scottie Scheffler, the defending champion and World No. 1, found himself in a distant fifth place at 12-under-par, four shots behind the leaders , . This positioning set the stage for a thrilling Sunday afternoon, where the fate of the FedEx Cup would be decided by the player with the lowest final-round score.

The final round, played on Sunday, August 24, 2025, lived up to the anticipation, delivering moments of brilliance and resilience from multiple contenders , . Tommy Fleetwood began his charge early, birdying the par-3 15th hole to overcome a double bogey earlier in his round and then picking up consecutive birdies on the 16th and 17th holes to solidify his grip on the lead . He closed out his round with a steady 6-under-par 68, finishing the tournament at 18-under-par 262, a score that proved insurmountable for his rivals , . Meanwhile, Patrick Cantlay staged a remarkable comeback effort. After a slow start, he surged down the stretch, carding four birdies on his final five holes to finish with a scintillating 6-under-par 64 . Though his incredible closing round propelled him into contention, it was not enough to catch Fleetwood, who maintained his composure under pressure. Russell Henley also delivered a strong performance, firing a 69 to finish in a three-way tie for second place alongside Cantlay, at 15-under-par 261 , .

Throughout the day, several other top players put forth valiant efforts but ultimately fell short of contending for the title. Scottie Scheffler, despite being a heavy favorite entering the week, failed to make a significant impact in the final round, settling for a 66 to finish tied for fourth at 14-under-par , . This result highlighted the impact of the new format, which erased the pre-tournament seeding advantages that had previously given Scheffler an edge . Other notable performances included those of Rory McIlroy, who finished at -6, and Justin Thomas, who placed T7 , . The tournament also featured the debuts of seven players, including Maverick McNealy, Harry Hall, and Akshay Bhatia, though none advanced beyond the weekend . The final leaderboard reflected the high level of competition, with payouts extending down to 30th place, demonstrating the immense value of simply qualifying for the event . The victory belonged unequivocally to Tommy Fleetwood, whose consistent play over four rounds secured him the $10 million prize and the FedEx Cup title, cementing his status as the season's champion , .

## The Champion: Tommy Fleetwood's Historic Triumph

Tommy Fleetwood of England etched his name into the annals of professional golf by winning the 2025 Tour Championship, a victory that was both a long-awaited personal milestone and a historic achievement in the context of the FedEx Cup , . With a final-round score of 6-under 68, Fleetwood completed the tournament at 18-under-par 262, securing his first-ever PGA Tour victory , . This triumph was particularly poignant as it came in his 164th start on the tour, signaling the fulfillment of a career-long quest for a signature win , . His victory was decisive, as he finished three shots clear of the field, defeating a pair of fellow Ryder Cup hopefuls, Patrick Cantlay and Russell Henley, who shared the runner-up spot at 15-under-par 261 , . The win was not just about claiming the tournament trophy; it also bestowed upon Fleetwood the FedEx Cup title, completing the season's grand slam of honors , .

Perhaps the most remarkable aspect of Fleetwood's victory was its historical significance. He became the first player since the inception of the FedEx Cup in 2007 to win both the TOUR Championship and the FedEx Cup in their very first PGA Tour victory . This dual accomplishment places his win in a class of its own, distinguishing it from the achievements of every other champion from 2007 to 2024 . While many players have gone on to win majors or other WGC events after capturing the FedEx Cup, no one had managed to achieve the feat of winning the crown in their maiden tour win until Fleetwood. This achievement underscores the immense difficulty of the Tour Championship, especially under the newly reinstated "clean slate" format, where players are forced to earn every shot from the first tee without any initial advantage . By prevailing in this unforgiving environment, Fleetwood demonstrated a level of skill and mental fortitude that resonated throughout the golfing world.

Fleetwood's path to victory was a testament to his consistency and ability to perform under pressure. After opening with a strong second-round 63, he navigated the challenges of the final two rounds with poise, rebounding from a double bogey on the 15th hole during the third round with back-to-back birdies on the 16th and 17th holes to maintain his lead , . His final-round performance was masterful, as he methodically picked off shots to build his three-shot lead heading into the homestretch. His victory was celebrated widely, and his win was recognized as a major step forward in his career. The win also carried significant implications for international golf, as he joined the exclusive club of European-born FedEx Cup champions, a group that includes legends like Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy . By becoming the 19th player to win the FedEx Cup, Fleetwood solidified his legacy and positioned himself as one of the game's premier talents . His journey from a promising talent to a seasoned veteran finally culminating in this historic victory provides a powerful narrative of perseverance and excellence.

## Prize Money and Financial Structure

The financial landscape of the 2025 Tour Championship underwent a significant restructuring, reflecting the PGA Tour's broader realignment of the FedEx Cup Playoffs . The total prize purse for the tournament was set at $40 million, a substantial decrease from the $75 million purse of the 2024 event and the $100 million bonus pool distributed in previous years , , . Consequently, the winner's share was reduced to $10 million, down from the record-breaking $25 million offered to Scottie Scheffler in 2024 , . This reduction was not an arbitrary cut but rather a direct result of a strategic decision to redistribute portions of the total FedEx Cup bonus pool to the earlier events in the playoff schedule , . Specifically, the PGA Tour allocated $60 million of the total $100 million FedEx Cup bonus pool to be paid out at the Wyndham Championship and the BMW Championship, leaving only $40 million to be distributed based on finishing positions at the Tour Championship itself , .

This new distribution model fundamentally changed the economic dynamics of the playoffs. Instead of concentrating the majority of the bonus at the final event, the revised structure rewards season-long performance more directly. For instance, the No. 1-ranked player in the FedEx Cup standings after the regular season received a $10 million payout, and the No. 1 seed after the BMW Championship was guaranteed a $5 million bonus before the final tournament even began , . This meant that the potential total earnings for a FedEx Cup winner could reach as high as $33 million if they combined a top-five finish at the Tour Championship with strong performances leading up to it . The $10 million awarded to the winner of the 2025 Tour Championship was classified as official prize money for winning the tournament, while the remaining $10 million of the total FedEx Cup bonus was paid separately . This structure was designed to make the FedEx Cup "the most difficult to win" by ensuring that qualification for the Tour Championship itself was a significant reward for consistent play throughout the season , .

*Note: The exact payout amounts for some positions vary slightly between sources, likely due to rounding differences in prize money calculations , . The above figures represent the most commonly cited amounts.*

Beyond the cash prizes, a Tour Championship victory carries additional significant benefits. Winners receive a five-year PGA Tour exemption, providing them with guaranteed entry into tournaments for the next five seasons . Furthermore, the FedEx Cup champion earns a $10 million bonus, bringing the total financial reward for the season's pinnacle event to $20 million, plus any other bonuses like the Comcast Business top 10 award . This comprehensive package of financial rewards, tournament exemptions, and the prestige of the title makes the Tour Championship the most lucrative and important event on the PGA Tour calendar.

## Legacy and Historical Context

The 2025 Tour Championship will be remembered as a watershed moment that reshaped the future of the FedEx Cup Playoffs. Its most enduring legacy is the successful reversion to a traditional 72-hole stroke-play format, a decision that restored clarity and competitive integrity to the season's finale , . By eliminating the "Starting Strokes" system, the PGA Tour responded decisively to years of player and fan feedback, reaffirming its commitment to rewarding the best player over 72 holes of competition , . This change was not merely cosmetic; it recalibrated the FedEx Cup to be a true reflection of season-long merit, making the Tour Championship the ultimate and most challenging tournament to qualify for . The success of this new format, coupled with a more demanding course setup at East Lake, signaled a new era for the playoffs—one focused on simplicity, challenge, and enhanced prestige , .

On the course, the tournament's legacy is defined by the historic victory of Tommy Fleetwood. His triumph was more than just a win; it was a statement of his arrival as a dominant force in world golf. By winning both the TOUR Championship and the FedEx Cup in his first PGA Tour victory, Fleetwood joined an elite pantheon of champions and broke a long-standing pattern in the event's history . His performance stands as a benchmark for consistency and resilience, particularly in a format where all players were on an equal footing from the outset . This clean-slate victory adds a layer of historical weight to his achievement, as it demonstrates that he was the best player over the entire four-day tournament, not just the best performer relative to his starting position. His win serves as a powerful narrative of perseverance, validating his long career with the sport's most coveted prize.

Looking back, the 2025 championship fits into a rich tapestry of FedEx Cup history that began in 2007 with Tiger Woods' inaugural victory , . Since then, the event has evolved through various formats, from reset points systems to the experimental "Starting Strokes" model introduced in 2019 , . The 2025 edition represents a critical pivot point, returning to a foundational principle of golf: the lowest score wins. The complete list of FedEx Cup champions from 2007 to 2023 showcases a roster of the game's greatest players, including Tiger Woods (twice), Vijay Singh, Jim Furyk, Rory McIlroy (three times), Justin Thomas, and Viktor Hovland , . By adding his name to this prestigious list, Tommy Fleetwood joins this illustrious company. The 2025 Tour Championship, therefore, not only crowned a deserving champion but also successfully navigated a significant structural evolution, ensuring the FedEx Cup remains the premier season-long competition in men's professional golf for years to come.

By becoming the 19th player to win the FedEx Cup, Fleetwood solidified his legacy and positioned himself as one of the game's premier talents.
His journey from a promising talent to a seasoned veteran finally culminating in this historic victory provides a powerful narrative of perseverance and excellence.
The financial landscape of the 2025 Tour Championship underwent a significant restructuring, reflecting the PGA Tour's broader realignment of the FedEx Cup Playoffs.
The total prize purse for the tournament was set at $40 million, a substantial decrease from the $75 million purse of the 2024 event and the $100 million bonus pool distributed in previous years.
Consequently, the winner's share was reduced to $10 million, down from the record-breaking $25 million offered to Scottie Scheffler in 2024.
This reduction was not an arbitrary cut but rather a direct result of a strategic decision to redistribute portions of the total FedEx Cup bonus pool to the earlier events in the playoff schedule.

Specifically, the PGA Tour allocated $60 million of the total $100 million FedEx Cup bonus pool to be paid out at the Wyndham Championship and the BMW Championship, leaving only $40 million to be distributed based on finishing positions at the Tour Championship itself.
This new distribution model fundamentally changed the economic dynamics of the playoffs.
Instead of concentrating the majority of the bonus at the final event, the revised structure rewards season-long performance more directly.

For instance, the No. 1-ranked player in the FedEx Cup standings after the regular season received a $10 million payout, and the No. 1 seed after the BMW Championship was guaranteed a $5 million bonus before the final tournament even began.

This meant that the potential total earnings for a FedEx Cup winner could reach as high as $33 million if they combined a top-five finish at the Tour Championship with strong performances leading up to it.

The $10 million awarded to the winner of the 2025 Tour Championship was classified as official prize money for winning the tournament, while the remaining $10 million of the total FedEx Cup bonus was paid separately.

This structure was designed to make the FedEx Cup "the most difficult to win" by ensuring that qualification for the Tour Championship itself was a significant reward for consistent play throughout the season.
The tiered payout structure for the 2025 Tour Championship is outlined in the table below, showing the prize money awarded to each finishing position.
All payouts are in U.S. dollars.
The 1st place payout was $10,000,000.
The T2 place payout was $4,352,500.
The T4 place payout was $2,616,666.67.
The T7 place payout was $1,121,666.67.
The T10 place payout was $750,000.
The T16 place payout was $450,000.
The 30th place payout was $355,000.
The exact payout amounts for some positions vary slightly between sources, likely due to rounding differences in prize money calculations.
The above figures represent the most commonly cited amounts.
Winners receive a five-year PGA Tour exemption, providing them with guaranteed entry into tournaments for the next five seasons.

Furthermore, the FedEx Cup champion earns a $10 million bonus, bringing the total financial reward for the season's pinnacle event to $20 million, plus any other bonuses like the Comcast Business top 10 award.
This comprehensive package of financial rewards, tournament exemptions, and the prestige of the title makes the Tour Championship the most lucrative and important event on the PGA Tour calendar.
The 2025 Tour Championship will be remembered as a watershed moment that reshaped the future of the FedEx Cup Playoffs.
Its most enduring legacy is the successful reversion to a traditional 72-hole stroke-play format, a decision that restored clarity and competitive integrity to the season's finale.

By eliminating the "Starting Strokes" system, the PGA Tour responded decisively to years of player and fan feedback, reaffirming its commitment to rewarding the best player over 72 holes of competition.

This change was not merely cosmetic; it recalibrated the FedEx Cup to be a true reflection of season-long merit, making the Tour Championship the ultimate and most challenging tournament to qualify for.
The success of this new format, coupled with a more demanding course setup at East Lake, signaled a new era for the playoffs—one focused on simplicity, challenge, and enhanced prestige.
On the course, the tournament's legacy is defined by the historic victory of Tommy Fleetwood.
His triumph was more than just a win; it was a statement of his arrival as a dominant force in world golf.
By winning both the TOUR Championship and the FedEx Cup in his first PGA Tour victory, Fleetwood joined an elite pantheon of champions and broke a long-standing pattern in the event's history.
His performance stands as a benchmark for consistency and resilience, particularly in a format where all players were on an equal footing from the outset.

This clean-slate victory adds a layer of historical weight to his achievement, as it demonstrates that he was the best player over the entire four-day tournament, not just the best performer relative to his starting position.
His win serves as a powerful narrative of perseverance, validating his long career with the sport's most coveted prize.
Looking back, the 2025 championship fits into a rich tapestry of FedEx Cup history that began in 2007 with Tiger Woods' inaugural victory.
Since then, the event has evolved through various formats, from reset points systems to the experimental "Starting Strokes" model introduced in 2019.
The 2025 edition represents a critical pivot point, returning to a foundational principle of golf: the lowest score wins.

The complete list of FedEx Cup champions from 2007 to 2023 showcases a roster of the game's greatest players, including Tiger Woods (twice), Vijay Singh, Jim Furyk, Rory McIlroy (three times), Justin Thomas, and Viktor Hovland.
By adding his name to this prestigious list, Tommy Fleetwood joins this illustrious company.

The 2025 Tour Championship, therefore, not only crowned a deserving champion but also successfully navigated a significant structural evolution, ensuring the FedEx Cup remains the premier season-long competition in men's professional golf for years to come.

2025 Tour Championship leaderboard: Tommy Fleetwood ties Russell Henley on top as Scottie Scheffler stalls
==========================================================================================================

Fleetwood will again try to nab his first PGA Tour win over the final 36 holes at East Lake Golf Club
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[![Image 210: Robby Kalland ](https://sportshub.cbsistatic.com/i/r/2016/05/04/92ab0efa-b540-4fe3-b796-df34067aec1d/thumbnail/80x80/b00ced5de43b8e160d5cdb8510a0bebc/robbykalland.png)](https://www.cbssports.com/writers/robby-kalland/)

By [Robby Kalland](https://www.cbssports.com/writers/robby-kalland/)

Aug 22, 2025 at 3:10 pm ET • 1 min read

Join the Conversation

Tommy Fleetwood is once again atop the leaderboard at a significant event going into the weekend, this as the Englishman continues pursuing his elusive first PGA Tour win. Fleetwood fired a second-round 63 to reach 13 under and take the lead alongside Russell Henley at the midway point of the Tour Championship.

Despite falling short in brutal fashion twice this season -- adding to a mounting list of lose calls throughout his career -- Fleetwood continues to play some of his best golf. After a strong 64 to put himself in contention after 18 holes, a Friday 63 featured more sensational ball-striking and putting with Fleetwood standing second in strokes gained across both categories this week.

Fleetwood did most of his damage on the back nine at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta, making six birdies and one bogey on the inward side to surge to the top of the leaderboard.

That included back-to-back birdies on the 17th and 18th to close out his round in style, particularly important makes or Fleetwood, who's had issues finishing out rounds in his career. At the St. Jude Championship two weeks ago, he bogeyed the 18th in the middle rounds, ending the tournament on a sour note given he lost by just one shot.

At East Lake, Fleetwood has birdied the par-5 18th twice already, perhaps building positive momentum on the closing holes that can help him Sunday as he tries to finally push himself over the finish line and into the winner's circle.

Fleetwood fell painfully short of his first career win at the Travelers Championship -- in addition to the St. Jude -- this year, but he's responded to those failures in admirable fashion. He has consistently spoken about continuing to putting himself in those positions, noting that the feeling of contending is unlike anything else in golf and the reason why they play the game.

It's one thing to say the right things after heartbreaking losses but quite another to learn from previous mistakes and put corrections into action. Fleetwood should again find himself in the pressure cooker of being among the final pairings heading into Sunday's fourth round. To ensure he pulls through, Fleetwood will have to continue posting low scores as soft conditions at East Lake are expected through the weekend. Players have taken advantage of the soft greens and been attacking pins thanks to the rain in Atlanta.

Henley, the 18-hole leader, will join Fleetwood in the last pairing on Moving Day. The former Georgia Bulldogs star stalled out a bit after his opening 61, only managing two birdies and a bogey on his front nine, but he matched Fleetwood with closing birdies on the 17th and 18th to maintain a share of the lead.

Close behind those two is Cameron Young, who posted the low round of the day with a 62 to insert himself into the mix at 11 under. Young has been playing fantastic golf in the second half of the season, recently picking up his first career win at the Wyndham Championship. His improvement on the greens has been the catalyst for his strong season, and that has continued this week. Young is fifth in putting to go along with being No. 1 in strokes gained on approach, firing a back nine 29 on Friday to charge into contention.

Surprisingly absent from the top of the chase group is Scottie Scheffler. The world No. 1 was in second place entering Round 2 but could not get anything going Friday in a disappointing afternoon of golf. Scheffler was wayward off the tee and missed a handful of putts that had him quite frustrated. He did birdie the last to shoot a 1-under 69, but he fell off the pace at 8 under and faces a five-shot deficit going into the weekend.

The leaders
-----------

**1\. Tommy Fleetwood, Russell Henley (-13):** At this point, there's an argument that Fleetwood is playing like the second-best player in the world over the last couple months -- especially in the first 54 holes of tournaments. The problem is Sundays. After faltering twice already this year despite holding late leads, Fleetwood will not be given the benefit of the doubt until he proves he can handle that closing pressure. Henley had an up-and-down start to his round and couldn't quite get it in gear until the back nine when he finally settled in and made some birdies. Even with a pedestrian 67, he's still tied for first, and his stellar history at East Lake -- along with his accuracy off the tee -- prove he was deserving of being one of the trending picks entering the tournament.

Contenders
----------

**3\. Cameron Young (-11)**  
**T4. Patrick Cantlay, Robert MacIntyre (-10)**  
**6\. Scottie Scheffler (-8)**  
**T7. Rory McIlroy, Justin Thomas, Shane Lowry, Chris Gotterup, Sam Burns, Ben Griffin, Akshay Bhatia (-7)**

There is a big gap between the top 5 on the leaderboard and the rest of the field, so it'll take something special from Scheffler in sixth or someone in the 7-under group to get in the mix. That is nevertheless an extremely talented group, which includes the top two in the world rankings, each of whom is more than capable of running up leaderboards on a whim.

Accuracy off the tee will be the question for Young over the remaining 36 holes, but he showed Friday what can happen when he finds the short grass consistently. He's hitting it as well as he ever has with the irons and is combining that with elite putting that makes him a real threat to win the $10 million top prize this week.

MacIntyre and Cantlay are also in the mix just three back. The big Scot has shaken off his Sunday struggles at the BMW Championship and is back in the mix. Cantlay, meanwhile, has been off the radar for awhile and looked like he'd fall back Friday until a furious finish with two birdies and an eagle to close out his second round to stay in contention.

2025 Tour Championship updated odds, picks
------------------------------------------

*   Tommy Fleetwood (9/4)
*   Russell Henley (12/5)
*   Scottie Scheffler (5-1)
*   Cameron Young (8-1)
*   Patrick Cantlay (12-1)
*   Robert MacIntyre (14-1)
*   Rory McIlroy (25-1)

It would be great for Fleetwood to finally get his first win and do so at the Tour Championship with such a massive payday on the line, but it's tough to buy him at that price. Young is the best value of this group at 8-1; he's been consistently great with ball-striking and putting, and nothing we saw from him Friday was fluky. Conditions aren't supposed to change much with more rain in the forecast this weekend, so a guy who can move it as far as he can off the tee and is as dialed as he is with the irons could absolutely take it low again on the weekend.

Updated Aug. 24, 2025, 6:11 p.m. ET

The [2025 Tour Championship](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/golf/pga/leaderboard/5008086) has 18 holes left on this Sunday. It's the final round of the tournament and the day of the [FedEx Cup Playoffs](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/golf/pga/fedex-cup).

No better place to be than right here to stay up-to-date with all the Sunday action. Follow along for a live leaderboard plus highlights, scores and more.

![Image 1: The FedEx Cup trophy at East Lake Golf Club.](https://golfweek.usatoday.com/gcdn/authoring/authoring-images/2025/08/18/SGLF/85717052007-usatsi-9564401.jpg?width=660&height=441&fit=crop&format=pjpg&auto=webp)

2025 Tour Championship live leaderboard
---------------------------------------

Stay on top of the scores all day with the [Golfweek/USA TODAY 2025 Tour Championship leaderboard](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/golf/pga/leaderboard/5008086).

Tommy Fleetwood wins 2025 Tour Championship.
--------------------------------------------

It is finished. Tommy Fleetwood is the Tour Championship winner and FedEx Cup champion.

Back to 3 ahead
---------------

A Patrick Cantlay bogey moves Tommy Fleetwood's lead to three with two to play.

Tommy Lad bogeys the 15th
-------------------------

One of the most difficult par 3s of the season, Tommy Fleetwood bogeys the 15th (playing it in 3 over on the weekend) and drops to 18 under, two clear of Patrick Cantlay, with three to play.

Fleetwood's lead is back to 3
-----------------------------

Deep breath, Fleetwood fans. His lead is three with five to play.

Adorable Keegan Bradley moment
------------------------------

There's never a bad time for family. Even in the middle of a tournament.

Final group receives Pace of Play warning
-----------------------------------------

Tommy Fleetwood and Patrick Cantlay are two holes out of position and have officially been giving a warning about their Pace of Play. Another violation would result in their group being put on the clock.

Scottie Scheffler gets within 2
-------------------------------

If he going to do it again? Scottie Scheffler, who hit his opening tee shot out of bounds, is now in a three-way tie or second at 15 under and two behind Tommy Fleetwood after a birdie on the par-4 14th. Four holes left to post a score for the world No. 1

Fleetwood's lead down to 1
--------------------------

How quickly things can change. Fleetwood led Patrick Cantlay by four shots two holes into the final round. Now, Fleetwood's lead is down to 1 after a bogey on the 10th while Cantlay makes birdie.

Buckle up.

Tommy Fleetwood increases lead to 3
-----------------------------------

is it finally happening? Tommy Lad buries another birdie on the seventh to move to 18 under and three clear of Keegan Bradley and Russell Henley. The driveable par-4 eighth is up next, too.

Basketball world cheering for Tommy Lad?
----------------------------------------

First Caitlin Clark, now LeBron James have posted on social media their support for Tommy Fleetwood in the pursuit of his first PGA Tour win.

Should Keegan Bradley be a Ryder Cup playing captain?
-----------------------------------------------------

Bradley is playing well enough to be on the Ryder Cup team and he's T-3 through five holes Sunday at Atlanta. But as captain, should be play? Vote below:

Akshay Bhatia is 4 under through 8, moves to solo fifth
-------------------------------------------------------

Bhatia is one of the hottest golfers during the early going. After opening with two pars, he went birdie-birdie-bogey-birdie-birdie-birdie to get to 12 under overall. He's five back and in solo fifth.

Patrick Cantlay opens bogey-double bogey
----------------------------------------

One of the 54-hole co-leaders birdied the second hole, while the other took a double bogey, which came on the heels of a bogey on his first hole. That gives Fleetwood a two-shot lead over Russell Henley and Patrick Cantlay's nightmare start has him now four shots off the lead. He had gone 29 straight holes without a bogey before Sunday.

Caitlin Clark shows support for Tommy Fleetwood
-----------------------------------------------

The WNBA's biggest star is putting her support behind Fleetwood. Minutes before he was set to tee off, Clark posted a message on X:

Scottie Scheffler's opening tee shot goes OB
--------------------------------------------

Scheffler started Saturday's round with back-to-back bogeys but went on to shoot 66. On Sunday, he sent his tee shot on No. 1 out of bounds but then rallied to make bogey after hitting his fourth from 200 yards to two feet.

Viktor Hovland is having the best start so far
----------------------------------------------

Hovland, the 2023 Tour Championship winner, is 3 under through six hole. He's enjoying the best start of anyone in the early going. Sitting at 10th in the European team's Ryder Cup rankings, Hovland fell short of one of the [six automatic qualifying spots](https://golfweek.usatoday.com/story/sports/golf/ryder-cup/2025/08/24/ryder-cup-2025-european-automatic-qualifiers-bethpage-black/85803436007/), which were finalized earlier in the day. But he still has an solid chance of being one of Luke Donald's six captain's picks, which will be announced Sept. 1.

Where to watch, stream, follow the Tour Championship
----------------------------------------------------

### Final round, Sunday, Aug. 24

11 a.m. ET to 6 p.m. ET, PGA Tour Live on [ESPN+](https://go.web.plus.espn.com/6eQWqK?subId3=story%2Fsports%2Fgolf%2Fpga%2F2025%2F08%2F24%2Ftour-championship-sunday-final-round-live-updates-scores-tee-times%2F85717029007_u53e3lVFQgixUPl3ggbiNYl)

11 a.m. ET to 1:30 p.m. ET, [Golf Channel](https://www.fubo.tv/stream/tv/?irad=343747&irmp=1205322&subId1=SMG&subId2=Golfweek&subId3=story%2Fsports%2Fgolf%2Fpga%2F2025%2F08%2F24%2Ftour-championship-sunday-final-round-live-updates-scores-tee-times%2F85717029007_u5lUUAJbqxYlFVibMZ7oI2P)

1 p.m. ET to 6 p.m. ET, PGA Tour Radio on SiriusXM

1:30 p.m. ET to 6 p.m., NBC and [Peacock](https://imp.i305175.net/Y9vDoJ?subId3=story%2Fsports%2Fgolf%2Fpga%2F2025%2F08%2F24%2Ftour-championship-sunday-final-round-live-updates-scores-tee-times%2F85717029007_u5IU7B2PoeqNsJzOrAOIx32)

[Watch Golf Channel for free on Fubo](https://www.fubo.tv/stream/tv/?irad=343747&irmp=1205322&subId1=SMG&subId2=Golfweek&subId3=story%2Fsports%2Fgolf%2Fpga%2F2025%2F08%2F24%2Ftour-championship-sunday-final-round-live-updates-scores-tee-times%2F85717029007_u5AxO2lY6MgozMmMAYoZFZM) [Sign up for ESPN+ to watch PGA Tour Live](https://go.web.plus.espn.com/6eQWqK?subId3=story%2Fsports%2Fgolf%2Fpga%2F2025%2F08%2F24%2Ftour-championship-sunday-final-round-live-updates-scores-tee-times%2F85717029007_u5q7VeBEJBl2NFPqxEBl7oF) [Sign up for Peacock to stream PGA Tour](https://imp.i305175.net/Y9vDoJ?subId3=story%2Fsports%2Fgolf%2Fpga%2F2025%2F08%2F24%2Ftour-championship-sunday-final-round-live-updates-scores-tee-times%2F85717029007_u5AOVmZEBQ3sVBpsIIB2Q7z)

Tour Championship weather forecast
----------------------------------

The PGA Tour announced preferred lies will once again be in effect for Sunday's final round.

How much does the Tour Championship winner get?
-----------------------------------------------

The first-place prize at East Lake is $10 million. The winner is also named the FedEx Cup champion. He will receive a five-year PGA Tour exemption as well. The top seven-finishers will make north of seven figures. Last place is good for $355,000.

East Lake ties for No. 4 on Golfweek's Best list of [the top private courses in Georgia](https://golfweek.usatoday.com/story/sports/golf/2025/06/09/golfweeks-best-top-ranked-private-golf-clubs-each-state/83731361007/) and ties for No. 85 among [all classic courses in the U.S.](https://golfweek.usatoday.com/story/sports/golf/2025/06/23/golfweeks-best-2025-classic-top-200-golf-courses-united-states-ranked/83863202007/)

Tommy Fleetwood, Patrick Cantlay tied for TOUR Championship lead in search of FedExCup
======================================================================================

4 Min Read

[Daily Wrap Up](https://www.pgatour.com/news/daily-wrapup)

![Image 22: Tommy Fleetwood bounces back with birdie to tie lead at TOUR Championship](https://res.cloudinary.com/pgatour-prod/image/fetch/h_900,w_1600,c_fit/https://cf-images.us-east-1.prod.boltdns.net/v1/static/6082840763001/10e8691d-0e8b-4341-be6f-5a7d91975f5c/3044e449-a055-4470-a336-962b6f2370f3/1600x900/match/image.jpg)

Tommy Fleetwood bounces back with birdie to tie lead at TOUR Championship

* * *

* * *

Written by Associated Press

ATLANTA (AP) — One swing cost Tommy Fleetwood the lead Saturday in the TOUR Championship. Another great closing stretch gave Patrick Cantlay a shot at the ideal ending to three years without winning.

Cantlay birdied four of the last five holes on a rain-soaked course at East Lake Golf Club for a 6-under 64 and a share of the lead with Fleetwood, who rebounded from his double bogey on the par-3 15th hole with a pair of birdies for a 67.

And still the most compelling name of all is Ryder Cup Captain Keegan Bradley, who has until Wednesday to decide if he should pick himself for the U.S. team and made a compelling case with a 63 that left him very much in the mix.

Bradley is consumed with the Ryder Cup, and it didn't help that when he registered for the TOUR Championship, he saw the Ryder Cup bag of Arnold Palmer from the 1963 matches at East Lake. He was the last playing captain in the Ryder Cup.

  

![Image 23: Keegan Bradley ends day with birdie at TOUR Championship](https://res.cloudinary.com/pgatour-prod/image/fetch/h_900,w_1600,c_fit/https://cf-images.us-east-1.prod.boltdns.net/v1/static/6082840763001/3e7f958f-efc3-49cf-8683-81fe4d051a42/fb0ab08b-6a9b-4477-8e80-373f76968134/1600x900/match/image.jpg)

Keegan Bradley ends day with birdie at TOUR Championship

  

“It was really weird looking at it,” Bradley said. “Like really strange. Because I’m nowhere in the world of Arnold Palmer and somehow I’m in this with him right now.”

Throw in Russell Henley and Scottie Scheffler, and Sunday is shaping up as a thriller to conclude the PGA TOUR season with more than one cup in the conversation.

In a FedExCup finale in which no started with an edge in points or shots, it comes down to those five players separated by four shots, with Cameron Young (71) six behind.

Fleetwood ran off four straight birdies on the front nine, and he appeared to be in control after a wedge into 6 feet for birdie on the 13th. Then came the 15th, 220 yards to a peninsula green. From a shorter tee, only one tee shot went into the water each of the first two rounds.

Fleetwood was the 10th player to hit into the water Saturday, a 6-iron he knew was wet when it left his club. Even so, the congenial Englishman didn't let that ruin his round, answered with a pitching wedge from the bunker to 12 feet for birdie on the 16th.

  

![Image 24: Tommy Fleetwood bounces back with birdie to tie lead at TOUR Championship](https://res.cloudinary.com/pgatour-prod/image/fetch/h_900,w_1600,c_fit/https://cf-images.us-east-1.prod.boltdns.net/v1/static/6082840763001/10e8691d-0e8b-4341-be6f-5a7d91975f5c/3044e449-a055-4470-a336-962b6f2370f3/1600x900/match/image.jpg)

Tommy Fleetwood bounces back with birdie to tie lead at TOUR Championship

  

He failed to birdie the par-5 18th, leaving him in a tie with Cantlay at 16-under 194.

Cantlay won the FedExCup in 2021. He hasn't won since the BMW Championship in 2022, though he never looks too far off his game. One change was working with putting guru Phil Kenyon two weeks ago on his setup, and perhaps that's the spark.

“It's nice to close the way I did, especially the last two days,” Cantlay said. “I'm pleased with where I'm at.”

Cantlay might have assured his spot at Bethpage Black. Even at 15th in the Ryder Cup standings, he was seen as logical choice given how he performed under pressure in Rome and at the Presidents Cup last year in Montreal.

Now he has a chance to win the FedExCup for the second time.

“It’s always nice to have your game shape up at the end of the year, but like I said, I’m focused 100% on this week, and we’ll worry about the Ryder Cup a little later,” he said.

For Fleetwood, it's another shot at his first PGA TOUR title after gut-punching losses at the Travelers Championship and the FedEx St. Jude Championship two weeks ago. All he wanted was another chance, and this is another great one.

Henley went quiet on the back nine until a birdie on the final hole for a 69, leaving him two shots behind.

  

![Image 25: Scottie Scheffler sinks long birdie putt from the fringe at TOUR Championship](https://res.cloudinary.com/pgatour-prod/image/fetch/h_900,w_1600,c_fit/https://cf-images.us-east-1.prod.boltdns.net/v1/static/6082840763001/43fcff70-b03f-4a1f-ad10-6b4f8d369a89/bede6296-576a-4c5c-8c41-d5b0620911a8/1600x900/match/image.jpg)

Scottie Scheffler sinks long birdie putt from the fringe at TOUR Championship

  

Scheffler was so frustrated with putts he felt he slightly misread that he tossed his putter at his bad after missing an 8-foot birdie try on the 16th. He had missed two other birdie chances from slightly closer. He still shot 66, his 20th consecutive round under par.

“Felt like another frustrating day,” Scheffler said. "I felt like I did some things well out there. I was just a little bit off on my reads most of the day. I hit some good putts that just didn’t fall. Overall, I didn’t shoot myself out of the tournament, which making bogeys around this place can very easily do that.

“Proud of the turnaround,” he said. “But man, I wish I could have gotten a little bit more out of the round.”

Sunday is for the FedExCup and the $10 million prize, a chance for Scheffler to become the first repeat FedExCup champion, for Fleetwood to finally get that first PGA TOUR title, for Bradley to make it virtually impossible not to pick himself.

He already has two wins in the last 13 months, as many as any American this side of Scheffler.

“I’m either going to win or I’m not and we’re going to know the picks,” Bradley said. “We’re pretty confident with the picks that we have. One more day of golf to kind of finalize this whole thing, and I can’t wait. I’m done with this whole process. I want it over with either way.”

Tommy Fleetwood wins TOUR Championship for first PGA TOUR title, FedExCup
=========================================================================

4 Min Read

[Daily Wrap Up](https://www.pgatour.com/news/daily-wrapup)

![Image 22: Tommy Fleetwood's interview after capturing first win at TOUR Championship](https://res.cloudinary.com/pgatour-prod/image/fetch/h_900,w_1600,c_fit/https://cf-images.us-east-1.prod.boltdns.net/v1/static/6082840763001/08be1e82-61a9-4e30-9d1f-f934742c7f52/85883560-f6dd-4c30-967b-ce42edea9431/1600x900/match/image.jpg)

Tommy Fleetwood's interview after capturing first win at TOUR Championship

A

Change Text Size

* * *

* * *

Written by Associated Press

ATLANTA (AP) — Tommy Fleetwood of England ended a summer of heartache with the richest prize on the PGA TOUR. He won the TOUR Championship on Sunday for his first tour title to capture the FedExCup and its $10 million reward.

Fleetwood got plenty of help at the start when Patrick Cantlay began bogey-double bogey and could never catch up. Scottie Scheffler hit his opening tee shot out of bounds and still was a threat until a tee shot into the water ended his hopes on the 15th.

Through it all, Fleetwood held his nerve. He closed with a 2-under 68 for a three-shot victory over Cantlay (71) and Russell Henley (69).

“I’ve been a PGA TOUR winner for a long time, it’s just always been in my mind,” Fleetwood said. “A lot of close calls, but I’ve always enjoyed the challenge.”

His first PGA TOUR victory came with two trophies — the FedExCup and the “Calamity Jane” replica putter for the TOUR Championship.

  

![Image 23: Tommy Fleetwood closes out first TOUR win at East Lake, wins FedExCup](https://res.cloudinary.com/pgatour-prod/image/fetch/h_900,w_1600,c_fit/https://cf-images.us-east-1.prod.boltdns.net/v1/static/6082840763001/c4a66bd7-d911-427a-810a-102692f272b1/6e556f4b-a492-411d-8886-da291d9ecd7a/1600x900/match/image.jpg)

Tommy Fleetwood closes out first TOUR win at East Lake, wins FedExCup

  

Ryder Cup Captain Keegan Bradley was within one shot of the lead on the front nine but wound up with a 70 to tie for seventh. He now has to decide whether to use one of his six captain’s picks on himself. He announces his picks Wednesday.

But this day, this moment, belonged to Fleetwood, enormously popular around the world for coping with so many close calls with a refreshing perspective and joy for those who beat him.

An eight-time winner around the world, no stranger to big stages at the Ryder Cup or his silver medal at the Olympics last summer, Fleetwood was constantly reminded about his failure to win on golf’s strongest circuit.

He saw a one-shot lead turn into a one-shot loss at the Travelers Championship when he took three putts from the front of the green and Bradley made birdie. Fleetwood let a two-shot lead with three holes to play get away from him at the FedEx St. Jude Championship to start the postseason.

For all the hurt, he never lost hope.

  

![Image 24: Tommy Fleetwood's interview after capturing first win at TOUR Championship](https://res.cloudinary.com/pgatour-prod/image/fetch/h_900,w_1600,c_fit/https://cf-images.us-east-1.prod.boltdns.net/v1/static/6082840763001/08be1e82-61a9-4e30-9d1f-f934742c7f52/85883560-f6dd-4c30-967b-ce42edea9431/1600x900/match/image.jpg)

Tommy Fleetwood's interview after capturing first win at TOUR Championship

  

“Tomorrow might be my time, it might not,” he said Saturday evening before his third try going into the final round with no one in front of him. “But I’ll still have a great time doing it.”

He had a blast at East Lake, thousands of fans surrounding the green of a 34-year-old from England, all of them chanting, “Tommy! Tommy! Tommy!”

Fleetwood removed his cap, looked to the cloudy sky and let those long locks flow as he let out a yell.

Finally, Fleetwood.

“This wasn’t the most comfortable I’ve been,” Fleetwood said with a smile. “I feel like I’ve had a great attitude throughout it all. ... I’m so happy I got it done.”

He started tied for the lead with Cantlay, the FedExCup champion from 2021, searching for his first win in three years. He made bogey on the first, and then three-putted for double bogey on the second and suddenly was four behind.

Cantlay never went away, however, and a two-shot swing on the 10th — Fleetwood made bogey from the left rough, Cantlay made a 5-foot birdie — narrowed the gap to one shot. The next three holes were pivotal.

Cantlay failed to get on the green from a bunker on the par-3 11th and made bogey. Fleetwood birdied the next two holes with wedges to the 6-foot range, and Cantlay could only match one of them.

  

![Image 25: Tommy Fleetwood makes back-to-back birdies at TOUR Championship](https://res.cloudinary.com/pgatour-prod/image/fetch/h_900,w_1600,c_fit/https://cf-images.us-east-1.prod.boltdns.net/v1/static/6082840763001/3482baac-799c-49c7-891f-12eb912c2957/130c6e2b-be8f-4e84-b13c-a764f01c727c/1600x900/match/image.jpg)

Tommy Fleetwood makes back-to-back birdies at TOUR Championship

  

The last big hurdle was the 218-yard 15th to a peninsula green, where Fleetwood went in the water Saturday and made double bogey. This time, he managed a bogey and didn’t miss a step the rest of the way in finishing at 18-under 262.

Henley went 13 straight holes without a birdie and couldn’t put any serious pressure on him.

Scheffler’s start was even more shocking. His tee shot went left and disappeared under a fence, out of bounds. Then, he got up and down from 201 yards to salvage a bogey. He ran off three birdies in four holes to finish the turn, making a 40-foot birdie putt on the par-3 ninth.

But he missed a 5-foot birdie on the 10th, and his hopes ended with a 5-iron that went into the water on the 15th for double bogey.

There’s no doubting the best this year. Scheffler won five times, including two majors. He finished the season with 21 consecutive rounds in the 60s, and he has gone five straight months finishing no worse than fifth. He was trying to become the first back-to-back FedExCup champion.

“I battled all week to give myself a chance. I wasn’t as sharp as I would have hoped to have,” Scheffler said. “I had a good first round, but outside of that didn’t really play my best the first few days. Still gave myself a shot. Just needed a few better swings.”

* Written by Rob Bolton ### Tommy Fleetwood earns $10 million, wins FedExCup with first PGA TOUR victory at TOUR Championship Attaboy, Tommy! After enduring too many close calls that drove his narrative for far too long on the PGA TOUR, Tommy Fleetwood saved his best for the last tournament of the 2025 FedExCup season and prevailed at the TOUR Championship that concluded the FedExCup Playoffs. Fleetwood posted 18-under 262 to win by three strokes over Patrick Cantlay and Russell Henley at East Lake Golf Club. It is, of course, Fleetwood’s first victory in 164 PGA TOUR starts, but it’s a biggie because it means that he’s the 19th FedExCup champion. With no FedExCup points at stake in Atlanta, the entirety of his haul consists of $10 million in official earnings from a total prize fund of $40 million. _Scroll or swipe past the table below for more details of the outcome._

For live odds, visit_ [**_FanDuel_**](https://sportsbook.fanduel.com/golf)_._ Fleetwood’s personality, attitude and flowing locks are reasons why he’s adored by fans around the world, but his performances inside the ropes throughout the season cemented him as an underdog for the masses – he logged a T2, a T3, two T4s and a T5 among seven top 10s previously in 2025 – so his coronation on the PGA TOUR is celebrated beyond even the perimeter of his own orbit. The rub is that Fleetwood’s body of work muted his value in the betting market. At +1400 to win, he was third-shortest in the field of 30 pre-tournament at FanDuel. We might as well get used to it now that the seal has been broken. And while it hits as academic given his trajectory, it’s still notable to point out that the Englishman now is fully exempt as a FedExCup champion through his age-39 season of 2030. ![Image 23: Tommy Fleetwood's interview after capturing first win at TOUR Championship](https://res.cloudinary.com/pgatour-prod/image/fetch/h_900,w_1600,c_fit/https://cf-images.us-east-1.prod.boltdns.net/v1/static/6082840763001/08be1e82-61a9-4e30-9d1f-f934742c7f52/85883560-f6dd-4c30-967b-ce42edea9431/1600x900/match/image.jpg) Tommy Fleetwood's interview after capturing first win at TOUR Championship Fleetwood joins Chad Campbell (2003) as the only golfers in TOUR Championship history to capture their first TOUR title in the tournament. Fleetwood also follows Camilo Villegas (2008 BMW Championship) and Will Zalatoris (2022 FedEx St. Jude Championship) as first-time winners in the FedExCup Playoffs. Henley (+1800) opened the week with a tournament-best 61 to lead, and then shared the 36-hole pace with Fleetwood. Cantlay (+2500) made his move with a 64 in the third round after which he and Fleetwood co-led. The headliner upon arrival was, who else, Scottie Scheffler. He not only was bidding to win in consecutive weeks but he also was in position to become the first to win consecutive FedExCups for the first time. His measly odds of +150 reflected it, but [he settled for a three-way T4](https://www.pgatour.com/article/news/latest/2025/08/24/scottie-scheffler-ends-season-falls-short-of-fedexcup-ties-record-for-rounds-in-the-60s-east-lake-tour-championship), four strokes back of Fleetwood. 2025 Tour Championship Final Payouts, Prize Money: Tommy Fleetwood Wins $10 Million
===================================================================================

The Englishman picked the perfect week to finally break through on the PGA Tour.

#### [Jeff Ritter](https://www.si.com/author/jeff-ritter) | Aug 24, 2025

![Image 2: Tommy Fleetwood is a first-time PGA Tour winner and FedEx Cup champ.](https://images2.minutemediacdn.com/image/upload/c_crop,w_1917,h_1078,x_977,y_42/c_fill,w_720,ar_16:9,f_auto,q_auto,g_auto/images/ImagnImages/mmsport/si/01k3esemp1gwy1ptf0ty.jpg)

Tommy Fleetwood is a first-time PGA Tour winner and FedEx Cup champ. / Brett Davis-Imagn Images

[](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?app_id=531030426978426&display=popup&href=https:%2F%2Fwww.si.com%2Fgolf%2F2025-tour-championship-final-payouts-prize-money-pga-tour-season-finale)[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=2025%20Tour%20Championship%20Final%20Payouts%2C%20Prize%20Money:%20Tommy%20Fleetwood%20Wins%20$10%20Million&url=https:%2F%2Fwww.si.com%2Fgolf%2F2025-tour-championship-final-payouts-prize-money-pga-tour-season-finale)[](http://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https:%2F%2Fwww.si.com%2Fgolf%2F2025-tour-championship-final-payouts-prize-money-pga-tour-season-finale&title=2025%20Tour%20Championship%20Final%20Payouts%2C%20Prize%20Money:%20Tommy%20Fleetwood%20Wins%20$10%20Million)

* * *

The PGA Tour returned to Atlanta and East Lake Golf Club for its season-ending Tour Championship, offering a $40 million purse, with $10 million to the winner.

The Tour Championship [got a bit of a makeover this year](https://www.si.com/golf/pga-tour-stars-sharp-reactions-tour-championship-changes), with $100 million in season-ending prize money allocated differently than last year. In 2025, $60 million has already been dished out after the Wyndham Championship and BMW Championship. But the $40 million remaining is up for grabs, and the $10 million prize will technically count as official prize money, rather than a season-ending bonus.

In short, Tommy Fleetwood picked quite the week for his first PGA Tour win. The Englishman, having been so close in many events only to fall short, finished the job at East Lake to win and claim the FedEx Cup. His quest [captivated athletes across the sports world](https://www.si.com/golf/tommy-fleetwood-lebron-caitlin-clark-cheering-him-on-pga-tour-championship) and they all were happy Sunday night.

Here are the final payouts for the 2025 Tour Championship.

2025 Tour Championship Final Payouts
------------------------------------

**WIN:** Tommy Fleetwood, 18 under: $10 million

**T2.** Patrick Cantlay, Russell Henley, 15 under: $4,352,500

**T4.** Corey Conners, Scottie Scheffler, Cameron Young; 14 under: $2,616,666.75

**T7.** Justin Thomas, Sam Burns, Keegan Bradley; 13 under: $1,121,666.62

**T10.** Chris Gotterup, Ben Griffin; 12 under: $715,000

**12\.** Viktor Hovland, 11 under: $660,000

**T13.** Brian Harman, Harris English, Akshay Bhatia, Shane Lowry; 10 under: $570,000

**T17.** Harry Hall, Robert MacIntyre; 9 under: $482,500

**T19.** Collin Morikawa, Nick Taylor; 8 under: $452,500

**T21.** Justin Rose, Ludvig Aberg; 7 under: $422,500

**T23.** Rory McIlroy, Maverick McNealy; 6 under: $395,000

**T25.** J.J. Spaun, Andrew Novak; 4 under: $377,500

**T27.** Sungjae Im, Jacob Bridgeman; Even: $367,500

**29\.** Hideki Matsuyama, 3 over: $360,000

**30\.** Sepp Straka, 7 over: $355,000

* * *

2025 Tour Championship purse, prize money: Payouts for Tommy Fleetwood, field at FedEx Cup Playoffs
===================================================================================================

The final FedEx Cup purse was different than years past but still significant
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

[![Image 211: Patrick McDonald ](https://sportshub.cbsistatic.com/i/r/2025/11/11/acc97b44-6e88-46ac-838e-a1f4dac5bc8d/thumbnail/80x80/69f6b66523ac2aaff6304e56739f7182/screenshot-2025-11-11-at-11-17-05-am.png)](https://www.cbssports.com/writers/patrick-mcdonald/)

By [Patrick McDonald](https://www.cbssports.com/writers/patrick-mcdonald/)

Aug 24, 2025 at 6:08 pm ET • 1 min read

Join the Conversation

comments

![Image 212: fedex-cup.jpg](https://sportshub.cbsistatic.com/i/r/2025/08/24/5edcd0ce-13ae-4691-a619-2383fa71143b/thumbnail/770x433/73ba8e553b2edb3f88fb2d0fa469efe5/tommy-fleetwood-fedex-cup-trophy-g.jpg)

Getty Images

The final 72 holes of the 2025 PGA Tour season decided who took home the grand prize offered by the FedEx Cup Playoffs. While the 2025 Tour Championship again served as the season finale for the top 30 players on the PGA Tour, but the purse and prize funds looked different this season given the PGa Tour's decision to change the playing format for the final tournament.

Instead of the near-$83 million purse and $25 million winner's prize that had previously been dished out, the Tour Championship this year offered a $40 million purse with $10 million going to the winner, Tommy Fleetwood. Not bad considering this marked Fleetwood's first career win on the PGA Tour and he had just coughed up the lead at a prior playoff event two weeks earlier.

The rest of the FedEx Cup money had been doled out at various check points throughout this last month with those near the top of the FedEx Cup standings following the conclusion of play at the Wyndham Championship and BMW Championship getting rewarded handsomely. With some of that money already in the pockets of players, competitors at the Tour Championship were fighting for a bit less overall. Still, everyone who finished T8 or better cleared seven figures for their work in Atlanta, those who finished inside the top half of this 30-man field cleared $500,000.

That's a lot of money to throw around, of course, and [plenty has already been handed out](https://www.cbssports.com/golf/news/fedex-cup-earnings-how-much-each-golfer-in-the-2025-tour-championship-field-has-made-in-his-playing-career/) throughout the 2025 season. Let's take a look at how the $40 million sum got divided among the top 30 players on the PGA Tour this season.

How much? Here is the Tour Championship Prize Money for 2025
============================================================

[Matt Chivers![Image 5: Link](https://www.nationalclubgolfer.com/images/link.svg)](https://www.nationalclubgolfer.com/author/mchivers/)

[![Image 6: Facebook](https://www.nationalclubgolfer.com/images/social-facebook.svg)](https://www.facebook.com/NationalClubGolfer/)[![Image 7: X](https://www.nationalclubgolfer.com/images/social-x.svg)](https://x.com/ncg_com)[![Image 8: Instagram](https://www.nationalclubgolfer.com/images/social-instagram.svg)](https://www.instagram.com/nationalclubgolfer/?hl=en)[![Image 9: YouTube](https://www.nationalclubgolfer.com/images/social-youtube.svg)](https://www.youtube.com/user/NationalClubGolfer?sub_confirmation=1)[![Image 10: Podcast](https://www.nationalclubgolfer.com/images/social-podcast.svg)](https://www.nationalclubgolfer.com/podcasts/)[![Image 11: 0 comments](https://www.nationalclubgolfer.com/images/social-comment.svg)](https://www.nationalclubgolfer.com/tour/pga-tour/tour-championship-purse/#comments "0 comments")

### Table of Contents

The Tour Championship is the final event of the season and ends the FedEx Cup Playoffs. This is the finale to the 2025 schedule and will essentially crown the best player of the year.

So here is how the prize money works for the Tour Championship in 2025. In May, the PGA Tour announced that starting strokes would be removed from the Tour Championship format. Instead of a staggered scoring start, all 30 players will start on even par, and it is a 72-hole stroke play event.

The FedEx Cup Bonus Distribution is the same as 2024: $100 million. The winner of the FedEx Cup will get $10 million, which is the largest winner’s share of a tour event this season. The total prize purse for the Tour Championship is $40 million.

Below are images of how it works. As you can see, if a player held top spot at each Playoff event, they would earn $25 million, which is the same as what Scottie Scheffler won for taking the Tour Championship and FedEx Cup titles in 2024.

ALSO: [This is why the Tour Championship format has changed](https://www.nationalclubgolfer.com/tour/pga-tour/how-does-the-tour-championship-work/)

![Image 15: tour championship purse](https://www.nationalclubgolfer.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Screenshot-2025-08-01-142452.png)

**Signature Events**

The Arnold Palmer Invitational, the Memorial and the [Genesis Invitational](https://www.nationalclubgolfer.com/tour/pga-tour/genesis-invitational-preview/) were the player-hosted Signature Events that have 36-hole cuts and give away 20% of the purse to the tournament winner.

Here was the Signature Event schedule for the 2025 PGA Tour season. The Players Championship is not a Signature Event but offers 750 FedEx Cup points for the winner and a total purse of $25 million.

**The Sentry**: January 2 – 5  
Winner: Hideki Matsuyama

**AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am:** January 30 – Feb 2  
Winner: [Rory McIlroy](https://www.nationalclubgolfer.com/tour/player-profiles/rory-mcilroy/)

Winner: Sepp Straka

**Memorial Tournament:** May 29 – June 1  
Winner: Scottie Scheffler

**Travelers Championship:** June 19 – 22

FedEx Cup money, format, changes: How $100 million prize began
==============================================================

By: [Dylan Dethier](https://golf.com/writers/dylan-dethier/) August 24, 2025

*   Share on Facebook
*   Share on Twitter
*   Share by Email

![Image 2: Tiger Woods won the 2007 FedEx Cup.](https://golf.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/tigerwoods_2007fedexcup.jpg)

Tiger Woods won the 2007 FedEx Cup.

Getty Images

When the winner of Sunday’s Tour Championship lifts the trophy, he’ll have something in common with 2007 Tiger Woods: he’ll be walking away from East Lake Golf Club with a $10 million first-place FedEx Cup [prize](https://golf.com/news/2025-tour-championship-purse-payout-winners-share/).

But a whole lot else has changed. The venues are different. The fields have shrunk. And it looks a whole lot different than it did at the beginning. Let’s buzz through a quick history of the FedEx Cup Playoffs. No prize money included.

### 2007 — FedEx Cup Playoffs 1.0

**Prize fund**: $35 mil  
**First-place check**: $10 mil

**Format notes:** The PGA Tour first released its plans for a playoff in Nov. 2005, to be rolled out for the 2007 season. That first playoff year was a four-tournament setup; 144 players qualified for the first event, the Barclays, before cutting to 120 for the Deutsche Bank Championship, 70 for the BMW Championship and 30 for the Tour Championship.

**Fun fact**: Looking back, hosting these first three events outside New York (Westchester Country Club), Boston (TPC Boston) and Chicago (Cog Hill) before heading to Atlanta for the Tour Championship seems like a simple winning formula. Also it probably didn’t hurt that Phil Mickelson won the Deutsche Bank and Tiger Woods won the BMW _and_ Tour Championship.

### 2008 — FedEx Cup Playoffs 2.0 and 3.0

**Prize fund**: $35 mil  
**First-place check**: $10 mil

**Format notes:** In early 2008 changes were announced to the playoff points system, essentially juicing the points and punishing players who might be thinking of skipping the first event. (Woods had skipped the first-ever playoff event, the Barclays, the year prior.)

_After_ the 2008 playoffs, further points changes were announced for the 2009 season to guarantee that what had happened in 2008 — Vijay Singh building such a big lead that the FedEx Cup was decided before they’d even teed it up at the Tour Championship — wouldn’t happen again. The field for the first event was reduced to 125 players, followed by 100, 70 and 30.

**Fun fact**: It’s comical looking back at the first two winners, Woods and Singh, who finished with 123,033 and 125,101 FedEx Cup points, respectively; nobody cracked the 5,000-point marker in the decade that followed.

### 2019 — FedEx Cup Playoffs 4.0

**Prize fund:** $60 mil  
**First-place check:** $15 mil

**Format notes:** Here’s where everything changed. (Again.) The Tour reduced its number of events from four to three and moved the playoff’s dates up, finishing the final week of August and avoiding football in the process. That meant the Dell Technologies Championship (held in Boston) got axed. While 125 players still made the playoffs, they cut from 125 to 70 and then to 30.

This was also the beginning of the “Starting Strokes” era, in which the top-ranked player entering the Tour Championship earned an advantage to start the week, starting at 10 under par while second place would start at 8 under, third at 7 under, fourth at 6 under and on down to even par.

**Fun fact:** Remember when Tiger Woods won the Tour Championship in 2018 — and then that same night got on a flight to France for the 2019 Ryder Cup? That sort of thing doesn’t happen anymore, because the playoffs wrap up a month earlier.

### 2022 — FedEx Cup Playoffs 5.0

**Prize fund:** $75 mil  
**First-place check**: $18 mil

**Format notes:** No significant format changes, but 2022 was notable because it was LIV Golf’s first season, players were defecting left and right and the PGA Tour responded with _other_ format changes to its schedule (enter Signature Events) as well as various ways to get its players more money. That meant a bump to $75 million for the FedEx Cup, it meant increased purses and it meant ramping up the Player Impact Program (PIP) which would ultimately swell to $100 million on its own. (Also, for 2023, the field for the first playoff event was reduced to 70.)

**Fun fact:** Several of LIV’s players sued the PGA Tour for keeping them out of the FedEx Cup playoffs. Three players — Talor Gooch, Hudson Swafford and Matt Jones — tried to get a temporary restraining order to play the FedEx St. Jude Championship. It was ultimately denied.

### 2024 — FedEx Cup Playoffs 6.0

**Prize fund:** $100 mil  
**First-place check:** $25 mil

**Format notes:** If you increase prize money everywhere else (as with the Signature Events) you’d better juice up the playoff money to keep pace. Thanks in part to the sunsetting of the Player Impact Program, the Tour jacked up its prize money even further, sending $25 million to winner Scottie Scheffler.

**Fun fact:** $25 million is just a lot of money for winning a golf tournament.

### 2025 — FedEx Cup Playoffs 7.0

**Prize fund:** $100 mil  
**First-place check:** $10 mil (ish)

**Format notes:** The Tour ditched “Starting Strokes” and introduced a new FedEx finale format that was an awful lot like the pre-playoff edition of the Tour Championship: 30 players, low score wins.

But because the FedEx Cup is designed to reward season-long play, they spread payment across several tournaments instead of just dishing it out at the end of the season. That meant the No. 1-ranked Scheffler took home $10 million at the end of the regular season, plus $8 million for winning the Comcast Business Tour Top 10. Scheffler got another bonus of $5 million for remaining at that No. 1 spot after the BMW Championship. And he’ll have a chance at another $10 million if he can emerge the winner at the end of the Tour Championship.

**Fun fact:** Nice work, if you can get it.

It’s The TOUR Championship week – the final stop of the 2025 PGA Tour season, and while the field at East Lake is missing some familiar names, it still features a throng of marquee stars, including the season’s major winners: **Rory McIlroy** (Masters), **J.J. Spaun** (U.S. Open) and **Scottie Scheffler** (PGA and The Open).

The 30-player set will once again be contested at the historic East Lake Golf Club.

The star-studded gathering in Atlanta, Georgia will feature several former FedEx Cup winners, including Scheffler (2024), **Viktor Hovland** (2023), McIlroy (2022, 2019, 2016), **Patrick Cantlay** (2021), **Justin Rose** (2018), and **Justin Thomas** (2017).

Other top-ranked stars teeing it up this week in the Peach State include **Ludvig Aberg**, **Tommy Fleetwood**, **Collin Morikawa**, and **Hideki Matsuyama**, among others.

Below, you’ll find more details to help you get primed for the 2025 edition of the FedEx Cup’s TOUR Championship.

#### TOUR Championship History

[![Image 22: Tiger Woods](https://progolfweekly.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/img_5ba81334b23c8.png)](https://progolfweekly.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/img_5ba81334b23c8.png)

Tiger Woods celebrates on the 18th green after winning the TOUR Championship at East Lake GC on Sep. 23, 2018 in Atlanta, GA. Photo by Sam Greenwood/Getty Images

The Tour Championship has been the FedExCup playoff finale since the first playoff in 2007, but the event has roots going back 20 years earlier. Always an elite event, prior to 2007, its field consisted exclusively of the top 30 money leaders of the past PGA Tour season and generally took place in the late fall.

The inaugural 1987 event was claimed by **Tom Watson** – two strokes clear of **Chip Beck**, the second member of the 59 Club.

Other champions in the pre FedExCup era included legends such as **Curtis Strange**, **Tom Kite**, **Paul Azinger**, **David Duval**, **Tiger Woods** and **Phil Mickelson**.

In 2007, the Tour Championship moved from November to mid-September, where it ended the then four-tournament FedEx Cup Playoffs. As in past years, 30 players qualified for the event, but the basis for qualification was no longer prize money. Instead, FedEx Cup points accumulated during the regular PGA Tour season and then during the three preceding playoff events determined the participants.

[![Image 23: Rory McIlroy Wins 2022 FedEx Cup TOUR Championship](https://progolfweekly.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/2022-TOUR-Championship-Rory-McIlroy-Wins-3.jpg)](https://progolfweekly.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/2022-TOUR-Championship-Rory-McIlroy-Wins-3.jpg)

Rory McIlroy hoists the FedEx Cup after winning the TOUR Championship at East Lake GC on Aug 28, 2022 in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Tracy Wilcox for the PGA TOUR via Getty Images)

From 2019 onward, the FedExCup was reduced to three events, and the Tour Championship is now held in late August rather than mid-September. The tournament adopted a format called starting strokes in 2019, in order to ensure that the winner would also be the FedExCup champion. After much criticism, the format was shelved ahead of the 2025 finale and now plays as a traditional stroke-play championship.

Woods and McIlroy hold the tournament record with three wins – two coming in the FedExCup format, the most recent of which was in 2018. Mickelson is the only other player to have won more than one, with Tiger as the runner-up in both of Phil’s victories.

[![Image 24](https://progolfweekly.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/pgw-bobby-jones-charlie-yates.jpg)](https://progolfweekly.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/pgw-bobby-jones-charlie-yates.jpg)

Bobby Jones with good friend and mentor of Charlie Yates. Both played on the No. 1 & 2 Courses at East Lake. (Courtesy Charlie Yates GC)

East Lake Golf Club has been the Tour Championship’s permanent venue since 2004, although the FedEx Cup is only a small part of the club’s story. Founded 100 years earlier in 1904, the Atlanta course is a **Donald Ross** design, famous for being the home course of the legendary **Bobby Jones**.

It is believed to be the site where Jones played his first and last rounds. The course also once hosted the Ryder Cup, the 1963 edition, with **Arnold Palmer** as the U.S. captain.

#### Hole of the Week

[![Image 25: 2025 Tour Championship Primer Hole 15](https://progolfweekly.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/PGW-2025-Tour-Championship-Primer-Hole-15.jpg)](https://progolfweekly.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/PGW-2025-Tour-Championship-Primer-Hole-15.jpg)

A course scenic view as Dustin Johnson putts on the 15th hole green during the final round of the TOUR Championship, the final event of the FedExCup Playoffs, at East Lake Golf Club on September 25, 2016 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Keyur Khamar for PGA TOUR via Getty Images)

**No. 15**, East Lake Golf Club  
_Par 3, 211 yards_

Considered one of the oldest “isthmus” par 3s (not an island, but close to being one) in the country, the 15th hole at East Lake should once again provide all kinds of action this week. A super-flat green is surrounded by the golf course’s iconic lake, which provides a natural setting for gusts of wind to create havoc at most any time.

“The 15th hole will really be a gut-checking hole, as Justin Rose refers to some of the holes at East Lake,” Rees Jones said in 2016. “They will have to fight through 14 and 15 and then push the pedal down on the last three holes.”

The club’s signature hole has historically played well over par, and has ruined many good rounds down the stretch.
